Phone call from Springfield Tenant Union. Tenant union rep (J. Whitfield) referred a client, Maria Delgado. Maria Delgado referral_source Springfield Tenant Union. Record status: current. 2024-01-29 – 11:40 – RO
Voicemail from Maria Delgado (ph: 417-555-0134). She states she is the person referred by the Tenant Union. She says she can come to the office on Friday 2/2 at 10:00 AM. Left return call to confirm.

2024-01-30 – 14:05 – RO
Called Maria Delgado back at 417-555-0134. Confirmed appointment for 2/2 at 10:00 AM. She asked what to bring; advised photo ID, any lease or rental agreement, any notices from landlord, and proof of income if available. She said she has the lease and a notice about the water leak. She sounded anxious but cooperative.

2024-02-02 – 10:00 – RO
Intake meeting with Maria Delgado. Client is a Spanish-speaking woman in her 40s. Interview conducted in English; client's English is functional but she requested a Spanish interpreter for any court proceedings. Completed intake form (see file). Key details:
- Name on lease: Maria Delgado
- Current address: 1420 N. Grant Ave, Apt 3B, Springfield, MO 65803 (rental unit subject to lockout)
- Phone: 417-555-0134
- Employer: Midwest Bakery Supply, 2100 W. Chestnut St. (works as a packer, 32 hrs/wk)
- Household: client only (no dependents)
- Landlord: G. Hargrove, property managed by Hargrove Properties LLC
- Rent: $825/mo, due on the 1st; last paid 1/1/2024
- Issue: Water leak in bathroom ceiling reported 1/10; landlord did not repair; client withheld $200 of January rent and sent a written notice citing the condition. On 1/26 landlord changed the locks while client was at work. Client called police; police said it was a civil matter. Client has not been able to enter unit since; she has been staying with a coworker.
- Client has no prior evictions, no criminal record.
- Client does not have a copy of the written notice she sent to landlord; she says she kept a photo of it on her phone. Will send photo to us.

Client signed retainer for limited scope representation (eviction defense and lockout). No fee (income eligible). RO to check conflict of interest with Hargrove Properties (no prior matters on file). RO to request copy of lease from client.

2024-02-05 – 09:30 – RO
Called Hargrove Properties LLC (417-555-0198) to confirm ownership of the property at 1420 N. Grant Ave. Spoke with office manager, D. Simmons. She confirmed Hargrove Properties manages the building and that G. Hargrove is the owner. She said she was not aware of any lockout and would check with the owner. She asked if we were representing Ms. Delgado; I confirmed. She said she would have the owner call us. No further info obtained.

2024-02-06 – 11:15 – RO
Client sent photo of the written notice she gave to landlord (dated 1/15/2024). Notice states: "I am withholding $200 of January rent because the bathroom ceiling leak has not been repaired after I reported it on January 10. I will pay the full rent when the leak is fixed." Notice is signed by Maria Delgado. Photo saved to file.

2024-02-08 – 13:50 – RO
Left voicemail for G. Hargrove (ph: 417-555-0177) requesting return call regarding the lockout. No response by end of day.
Client also mentioned she has not received any written notice of eviction or termination. She believes landlord changed locks to force her out. She has keys that no longer work; she tried on 1/27 and 1/28. Police report number from 1/26: 24-003517 (Springfield PD). Client has a copy of the police report; will send photo.

Client’s check stubs from Bakery Supply (pay dates 1/15, 1/31, 2/15 not yet received). Hourly rate $14.50, 32 hrs/wk. Last stub (1/31) shows gross $1,856.00, net $1,482.10. No other income. Client has no bank account; she cashes checks at a check-cashing store. She has a prepaid debit card (NetSpend) for online purchases. No assets of note.

Client signed release for us to obtain her phone records if needed (to show she called landlord on 1/11 and 1/18). She said she called the main office number (417-555-0198) and left messages both times; no call back. She also sent a text to the owner’s cell (417-555-0177) on 1/20 asking about repair. No response. Screenshots saved.

Next steps:
- Draft emergency motion for temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction (re: lockout and access to retrieve personal property and cat).
- Send demand letter via certified mail to owner and property manager today.
- Request lease copy from client (she will look for it; she thinks she has a copy in her email).
- Check with court about emergency filing procedures for self-represented litigants; we will file on her behalf.

2024-02-10 – 11:40 – SW
Called client to confirm she received my email with the demand letter draft. She did not have access to a computer; she viewed it on her phone. She approved the language. Letter sent via certified mail, return receipt requested, to:
- G. Hargrove, 1420 N. Grant Ave., Springfield (property address, per lease)
- Hargrove Properties LLC, 2200 W. Division St., Springfield (registered office, per Secretary of State)

Sarah Whitfield is Maria Delgado's case worker. Record status: current.

Letter demands: (1) restore access to unit by 2/12; (2) allow supervised entry to retrieve personal property and cat; (3) repair ceiling leak within 72 hours; (4) confirm in writing that no eviction proceeding has been filed. Cites IL landlord-tenant law re: self-help eviction. Copy to file.

2024-02-12 – 09:15 – SW
No response from landlord or property manager as of this morning. Checked court docket for eviction case under client’s name (Maria Delgado, Maria Lopez, Maria Lopez-Delgado) – no case filed. Also checked for any case under property address – none.

2024-02-12 – 10:05 – SW
Called Hargrove Properties again (417-555-0198). Spoke with D. Simmons, office manager. She said she received our letter and “passed it to the owner.” She would not confirm whether owner intends to respond. I asked about access to retrieve the cat; she said she does not handle that and we need to talk to the owner directly. I asked for owner’s direct number; she said she would have him call. Noted.

2024-02-12 – 11:30 – RO
Per SW request, ran conflict check for Hargrove Properties LLC and G. Hargrove. No prior or current matters on file. Conflict check cleared.

2024-02-13 – 14:20 – SW
Filed emergency petition in Springfield Circuit Court (case no. 2024-CH-0188). Count I: preliminary injunction to restore possession (unlawful lockout). Count II: temporary restraining order to allow retrieval of personal property and pet. Count III: breach of implied warranty of habitability (for the leak). Attached: client affidavit, photos, police report, demand letter, certified mail receipt, lease (client found a copy in her email and forwarded it; lease dated 6/1/2023, term 12 months, rent $825/mo, landlord listed as G. Hargrove, property managed by Hargrove Properties LLC).
2024-02-14 – 08:40 – SW
Called client at 8:30. Cat is still inside the unit. She has been feeding it through the mail slot when possible, but landlord boarded the slot yesterday evening. She is very upset. I told her we filed the petition and hearing is set for 2/20. She said she will wait outside the unit tomorrow morning in case the owner shows up to let her in. I advised her not to enter through any window or door that is not the main entrance, and not to remove any boards herself. She agreed.

2024-02-14 – 09:05 – RO
Prepared notice of hearing for 2/20 at 10:00 a.m., Judge Albright, Courtroom 3B. Filed with clerk. Also emailed copy to D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties per her request. She replied within the hour: “Received, thank you.” No mention of owner.

2024-02-14 – 10:30 – SW
Client called again. Landlord’s maintenance man, who she knows only as “Tony,” came by and told her the owner wants to “settle this quietly.” He offered to let her in to get the cat if she signed a paper saying she would not sue. She did not sign. She has the paper – it’s a handwritten note on a piece of lined paper, not a formal document. I told her to keep it and not sign anything without showing me first. She will bring it in tomorrow.

2024-02-14 – 11:15 – SW
Spoke with attorney J. Marsh re: emergency petition. She will cover the 2/20 hearing if I am unavailable. Left file with her.

2024-02-15 – 09:00 – SW
Client came in with the handwritten note. Took photos. Note says: “I will let you in to get the cat, you sign you won’t sue me for anything. – G.H.” No date. No witness. I photographed it and returned the original to client. She said Tony is coming back this afternoon and she will tell him she needs to talk to me first.

2024-02-15 – 09:20 – RO
Checked circuit court records again. No new filings under any name variation for client or property. Also checked for any case under Hargrove Properties LLC – none.

2024-02-15 – 10:10 – SW
Phone call with client. She reports that Tony returned at 9:45 a.m. and she told him she cannot sign anything without her lawyer. He said “fine, then the cat stays in there.” She asked if she could at least get the cat’s food and litter box; he said no. She is crying on the phone. I told her we will ask the judge for an order allowing supervised entry to retrieve the cat and her belongings, and that I understand this is very stressful. She said she will try to wait until the hearing. I reminded her not to attempt entry on her own. She acknowledged.

2024-02-15 – 11:00 – SW
Prepared supplemental affidavit for client’s signature documenting the two offers from the landlord’s agent (2/14 and 2/15) and the refusal to allow retrieval of the cat. Will have client sign at the hearing or earlier if she comes in.

2024-02-15 – 14:30 – RO
Called Hargrove Properties re: service of the petition. D. Simmons confirmed receipt. She asked if the owner needs to appear at the hearing. I said he should, or an attorney for the company. She said she would “let him know.” No further questions.

2024-02-16 – 09:15 – SW
Client called. She is at the unit. The boards on the mail slot were removed overnight and the door is unlocked. She did not go in. She is waiting across the street. I told her to stay there and not enter. I called D. Simmons – she said she doesn’t know who removed the boards or unlocked the door, and that the owner is out of town. I asked if she could confirm whether the unit is legally vacant; she said she is not sure. I told her we will raise this at the hearing.

2024-02-16 – 09:40 – SW
Called client back. Told her to keep distance from the unit and not to enter even if the door appears open. She said she understands. She will wait until after the hearing.
2024-02-20 – 10:30 – SW
Client came in for scheduled meeting. We reviewed the supplemental affidavit (2/15) line by line. She signed it. Notarized by office manager. Original will be filed with the court today along with the petition. She confirmed she has not been back to the unit since 2/16 and has not spoken to Tony. She asked again about the cat. I repeated that we will ask for supervised entry as part of the emergency order. She said she understands.

2024-02-20 – 11:15 – SW
Filed petition for emergency order and supplemental affidavit at circuit court, 2nd floor clerk’s office. Case number assigned: 24CV-1187. Hearing set for 2/26 at 9:30 a.m., Judge M. Alvarez. I left a message for D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties with the hearing date and case number. She did not answer.

2024-02-20 – 14:00 – RO
Called court clerk to confirm service requirements for the emergency order. Clerk said petition must be served on the landlord/owner and any person in possession at least 48 hours before hearing. Since the owner is out of town, I asked about service by mail to the registered agent. Clerk said that is acceptable if we file proof of service before the hearing. I will prepare the certificate of service.

2024-02-21 – 09:05 – RO
Prepared certificate of service. Mailed copy of petition and supplemental affidavit to Hargrove Properties LLC, registered agent address on file with the Secretary of State. Sent certified mail, return receipt requested. Also faxed a copy to D. Simmons at the number she gave us on 2/15. Kept fax confirmation sheet.

2024-02-21 – 10:20 – SW
Client called. She said Tony called her this morning and told her he “threw the cat out.” She is very upset and wants to know if she can go look for it. I told her she may go to the alley behind the building and look, but she must not enter the unit or the yard if the gate is locked. She said she would check the alley and the parking lot. I asked her to call me when she gets back.

2024-02-21 – 11:40 – SW
Client called back. She found the cat in a carrier behind the dumpster in the alley. The carrier was closed but not locked. She took the cat to her sister’s house. She is relieved. I told her to keep the cat there and not bring it back to the unit. She said she will. I noted this in the file.

2024-02-22 – 15:30 – RO
Received certified mail receipt signed by someone at Hargrove Properties. The signature is illegible. I will bring the receipt to the hearing. Also checked court docket online – no response filed by landlord yet.

2024-02-23 – 09:00 – SW
Client called. She is worried about the hearing on Monday. She asked what to wear and what to say. I told her to wear something comfortable but neat, to speak only when the judge asks her a question, and to tell the truth. I reviewed the main points: the eviction notice, the two offers from the landlord’s agent, the refusal to let her retrieve her belongings, and the cat. She said she feels better.

2024-02-23 – 10:15 – RO
Called D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties to confirm she received the fax. She said she did and that the owner is “not happy about the cat thing.” She did not say anything else. I told her the hearing is 2/26 at 9:30 a.m. She said she would relay it.

2024-02-26 – 09:20 – SW
Arrived at courthouse with client. She was on time and seemed nervous but composed. We sat in the hallway. D. Simmons was there with a man I believe is the owner – she did not introduce him. No attorney present for Hargrove Properties.

2024-02-26 – 09:35 – SW
Hearing before Judge Alvarez. Client testified about the eviction notice, the offers from the landlord’s agent on 2/14 and 2/15, and the refusal to allow her to retrieve her belongings or the cat. I introduced the supplemental affidavit and the certified mail receipt. D. Simmons said the owner was out of town and that the unit was being cleaned out because the client “abandoned” it. Judge asked her if there was a written lease. She said no. Judge asked if the client had paid rent for February. She said no. Judge asked if the owner had filed an eviction action. She said no.
2024-02-26 – 10:30 – SW
After the hearing, client and I stepped into the hallway. Judge Alvarez said he would take the matter under advisement and issue a written order within five business days. I told client we should hear something by early March. She asked if she could go back to the unit to get the rest of her things. I said not yet – not until we have the order. She understood. She left with her sister, who had been waiting in the lobby. I will check the docket daily.

2024-02-26 – 11:15 – RO
Spoke with court clerk re: hearing outcome. Clerk confirmed no written order yet. Also asked about the procedure if the landlord files a late response. Clerk said the judge would consider it but the hearing already occurred. I will call the clerk again on Thursday if no order appears.

2024-02-27 – 09:05 – SW
Client called. She said the cat is doing well at her sister’s. She asked about the order. I told her nothing yet. She said the landlord’s agent called her yesterday and offered to let her pick up her belongings if she signed a release saying she “voluntarily surrendered” the unit. I told her not to sign anything and to refer the agent to me. She said she would. I called D. Simmons and left a message saying any communication should go through our office.

2024-02-27 – 14:20 – RO
Checked docket at 2:00 p.m. No order. Also searched for any new filings in the case – none. I will check again tomorrow morning.

2024-02-28 – 10:40 – SW
Client called again. She is anxious. She said she heard from a neighbor that the landlord had someone come and change the locks on the unit. I told her we will address that if the order goes in our favor. She said she is staying with her sister and has no plans to go back to the unit until we say it is okay. I reminded her not to sign anything from Hargrove Properties.

2024-02-28 – 11:05 – RO
Called D. Simmons to ask about the locks. She said the owner changed the locks because the unit was vacant and he wanted to secure it. I told her the client’s belongings are still inside and that changing the locks could be an issue if the court finds the eviction was improper. She said she would pass that along. No further comment.

2024-02-29 – 09:30 – SW
Checked docket at 9:00 a.m. No order yet. Client called at 9:15. She asked if there is a way to speed things up. I explained the judge has five business days and today is day three. She said okay. I told her I would call her the moment we hear anything.

2024-03-01 – 13:45 – RO
Docket check at 1:30 p.m. Still no order. I called the clerk’s office and spoke with M. Tran. She said Judge Alvarez had a heavy calendar this week and the order might come early next week. She noted the deadline is March 5. I thanked her.

2024-03-04 – 10:15 – SW
Client called. She is worried because it has been a week since the hearing. I told her the judge’s deadline is tomorrow and that we should hear something soon. She said she is running out of money and asked about emergency assistance. I gave her the number for the county social services office and told her to mention she is facing possible homelessness. She said she would call.

2024-03-04 – 14:00 – RO
Docket check at 1:45 p.m. No order. I will check again first thing tomorrow.

2024-03-05 – 09:10 – SW
Docket check at 9:00 a.m. Order entered this morning. Judge Alvarez ruled in favor of the client. He found that the landlord failed to follow proper eviction procedure, that the client did not abandon the unit, and that the landlord’s refusal to allow her to retrieve her belongings was unreasonable. He ordered that the client may return to the unit to collect her belongings and that the landlord must allow her access within 48 hours of her request. He did not award damages. I called client and gave her the news. She was very relieved and started to cry. I told her the next step is to request access to the unit.

Client signed release for us to obtain her phone records if needed (to show she called landlord on 1/11 and 1/18). She said she called the main office number (417-555-0198) and left messages both times; no call back. She also sent a text to the owner’s cell (417-555-0177) on 1/20 asking about repair. No response. Screenshots saved.

Next steps:
- Draft emergency motion for temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction (re: lockout and access to retrieve personal property and cat).
- Send demand letter via certified mail to owner and property manager today.
- Request lease copy from client (she will look for it; she thinks she has a copy in her email).
- Check with court about emergency filing procedures for self-represented litigants; we will file on her behalf.

2024-02-10 – 11:40 – SW
Called client to confirm she received my email with the demand letter draft. She did not have access to a computer; she viewed it on her phone. She approved the language. Letter sent via certified mail, return receipt requested, to:
- G. Hargrove, 1420 N. Grant Ave., Springfield (property address, per lease)
- Hargrove Properties LLC, 2200 W. Division St., Springfield (registered office, per Secretary of State)

Sarah Whitfield is Maria Delgado's case worker. Record status: current.

Letter demands: (1) restore access to unit by 2/12; (2) allow supervised entry to retrieve personal property and cat; (3) repair ceiling leak within 72 hours; (4) confirm in writing that no eviction proceeding has been filed. Cites IL landlord-tenant law re: self-help eviction. Copy to file.

2024-02-12 – 09:15 – SW
No response from landlord or property manager as of this morning. Checked court docket for eviction case under client’s name (Maria Delgado, Maria Lopez, Maria Lopez-Delgado) – no case filed. Also checked for any case under property address – none.

2024-02-12 – 10:05 – SW
Called Hargrove Properties again (417-555-0198). Spoke with D. Simmons, office manager. She said she received our letter and “passed it to the owner.” She would not confirm whether owner intends to respond. I asked about access to retrieve the cat; she said she does not handle that and we need to talk to the owner directly. I asked for owner’s direct number; she said she would have him call. Noted.

2024-02-12 – 11:30 – RO
Per SW request, ran conflict check for Hargrove Properties LLC and G. Hargrove. No prior or current matters on file. Conflict check cleared.

2024-02-13 – 14:20 – SW
Filed emergency petition in Springfield Circuit Court (case no. 2024-CH-0188). Count I: preliminary injunction to restore possession (unlawful lockout). Count II: temporary restraining order to allow retrieval of personal property and pet. Count III: breach of implied warranty of habitability (for the leak). Attached: client affidavit, photos, police report, demand letter, certified mail receipt, lease (client found a copy in her email and forwarded it; lease dated 6/1/2023, term 12 months, rent $825/mo, landlord listed as G. Hargrove, property managed by Hargrove Properties LLC).

documents.title: Case Notes Log – Maria Delgado
documents.content:
2024-02-14 – 08:40 – SW
Called client at 8:30. Cat is still inside the unit. She has been feeding it through the mail slot when possible, but landlord boarded the slot yesterday evening. She is very upset. I told her we filed the petition and hearing is set for 2/20. She said she will wait outside the unit tomorrow morning in case the owner shows up to let her in. I advised her not to enter through any window or door that is not the main entrance, and not to remove any boards herself. She agreed.

2024-02-14 – 09:05 – RO
Prepared notice of hearing for 2/20 at 10:00 a.m., Judge Albright, Courtroom 3B. Filed with clerk. Also emailed copy to D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties per her request. She replied within the hour: “Received, thank you.” No mention of owner.

2024-02-14 – 10:30 – SW
Client called again. Landlord’s maintenance man, who she knows only as “Tony,” came by and told her the owner wants to “settle this quietly.” He offered to let her in to get the cat if she signed a paper saying she would not sue. She did not sign. She has the paper – it’s a handwritten note on a piece of lined paper, not a formal document. I told her to keep it and not sign anything without showing me first. She will bring it in tomorrow.

2024-02-14 – 11:15 – SW
Spoke with attorney J. Marsh re: emergency petition. She will cover the 2/20 hearing if I am unavailable. Left file with her.

2024-02-15 – 09:00 – SW
Client came in with the handwritten note. Took photos. Note says: “I will let you in to get the cat, you sign you won’t sue me for anything. – G.H.” No date. No witness. I photographed it and returned the original to client. She said Tony is coming back this afternoon and she will tell him she needs to talk to me first.

2024-02-15 – 09:20 – RO
Checked circuit court records again. No new filings under any name variation for client or property. Also checked for any case under Hargrove Properties LLC – none.

2024-02-15 – 10:10 – SW
Phone call with client. She reports that Tony returned at 9:45 a.m. and she told him she cannot sign anything without her lawyer. He said “fine, then the cat stays in there.” She asked if she could at least get the cat’s food and litter box; he said no. She is crying on the phone. I told her we will ask the judge for an order allowing supervised entry to retrieve the cat and her belongings, and that I understand this is very stressful. She said she will try to wait until the hearing. I reminded her not to attempt entry on her own. She acknowledged.

2024-02-15 – 11:00 – SW
Prepared supplemental affidavit for client’s signature documenting the two offers from the landlord’s agent (2/14 and 2/15) and the refusal to allow retrieval of the cat. Will have client sign at the hearing or earlier if she comes in.

2024-02-15 – 14:30 – RO
Called Hargrove Properties re: service of the petition. D. Simmons confirmed receipt. She asked if the owner needs to appear at the hearing. I said he should, or an attorney for the company. She said she would “let him know.” No further questions.

2024-02-16 – 09:15 – SW
Client called. She is at the unit. The boards on the mail slot were removed overnight and the door is unlocked. She did not go in. She is waiting across the street. I told her to stay there and not enter. I called D. Simmons – she said she doesn’t know who removed the boards or unlocked the door, and that the owner is out of town. I asked if she could confirm whether the unit is legally vacant; she said she is not sure. I told her we will raise this at the hearing.

2024-02-16 – 09:40 – SW
Called client back. Told her to keep distance from the unit and not to enter even if the door appears open. She said she understands. She will wait until after the hearing.

documents.title: Case Notes Log – Maria Delgado
documents.content:
2024-02-20 – 10:30 – SW
Client came in for scheduled meeting. We reviewed the supplemental affidavit (2/15) line by line. She signed it. Notarized by office manager. Original will be filed with the court today along with the petition. She confirmed she has not been back to the unit since 2/16 and has not spoken to Tony. She asked again about the cat. I repeated that we will ask for supervised entry as part of the emergency order. She said she understands.

2024-02-20 – 11:15 – SW
Filed petition for emergency order and supplemental affidavit at circuit court, 2nd floor clerk’s office. Case number assigned: 24CV-1187. Hearing set for 2/26 at 9:30 a.m., Judge M. Alvarez. I left a message for D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties with the hearing date and case number. She did not answer.

2024-02-20 – 14:00 – RO
Called court clerk to confirm service requirements for the emergency order. Clerk said petition must be served on the landlord/owner and any person in possession at least 48 hours before hearing. Since the owner is out of town, I asked about service by mail to the registered agent. Clerk said that is acceptable if we file proof of service before the hearing. I will prepare the certificate of service.

2024-02-21 – 09:05 – RO
Prepared certificate of service. Mailed copy of petition and supplemental affidavit to Hargrove Properties LLC, registered agent address on file with the Secretary of State. Sent certified mail, return receipt requested. Also faxed a copy to D. Simmons at the number she gave us on 2/15. Kept fax confirmation sheet.

2024-02-21 – 10:20 – SW
Client called. She said Tony called her this morning and told her he “threw the cat out.” She is very upset and wants to know if she can go look for it. I told her she may go to the alley behind the building and look, but she must not enter the unit or the yard if the gate is locked. She said she would check the alley and the parking lot. I asked her to call me when she gets back.

2024-02-21 – 11:40 – SW
Client called back. She found the cat in a carrier behind the dumpster in the alley. The carrier was closed but not locked. She took the cat to her sister’s house. She is relieved. I told her to keep the cat there and not bring it back to the unit. She said she will. I noted this in the file.

2024-02-22 – 15:30 – RO
Received certified mail receipt signed by someone at Hargrove Properties. The signature is illegible. I will bring the receipt to the hearing. Also checked court docket online – no response filed by landlord yet.

2024-02-23 – 09:00 – SW
Client called. She is worried about the hearing on Monday. She asked what to wear and what to say. I told her to wear something comfortable but neat, to speak only when the judge asks her a question, and to tell the truth. I reviewed the main points: the eviction notice, the two offers from the landlord’s agent, the refusal to let her retrieve her belongings, and the cat. She said she feels better.

2024-02-23 – 10:15 – RO
Called D. Simmons at Hargrove Properties to confirm she received the fax. She said she did and that the owner is “not happy about the cat thing.” She did not say anything else. I told her the hearing is 2/26 at 9:30 a.m. She said she would relay it.

2024-02-26 – 09:20 – SW
Arrived at courthouse with client. She was on time and seemed nervous but composed. We sat in the hallway. D. Simmons was there with a man I believe is the owner – she did not introduce him. No attorney present for Hargrove Properties.

2024-02-26 – 09:35 – SW
Hearing before Judge Alvarez. Client testified about the eviction notice, the offers from the landlord’s agent on 2/14 and 2/15, and the refusal to allow her to retrieve her belongings or the cat. I introduced the supplemental affidavit and the certified mail receipt. D. Simmons said the owner was out of town and that the unit was being cleaned out because the client “abandoned” it. Judge asked her if there was a written lease. She said no. Judge asked if the client had paid rent for February. She said no. Judge asked if the owner had filed an eviction action. She said no.

documents.title: Case Notes Log – Maria Delgado
documents.content:
2024-02-26 – 10:30 – SW
After the hearing, client and I stepped into the hallway. Judge Alvarez said he would take the matter under advisement and issue a written order within five business days. I told client we should hear something by early March. She asked if she could go back to the unit to get the rest of her things. I said not yet – not until we have the order. She understood. She left with her sister, who had been waiting in the lobby. I will check the docket daily.

2024-02-26 – 11:15 – RO
Spoke with court clerk re: hearing outcome. Clerk confirmed no written order yet. Also asked about the procedure if the landlord files a late response. Clerk said the judge would consider it but the hearing already occurred. I will call the clerk again on Thursday if no order appears.

2024-02-27 – 09:05 – SW
Client called. She said the cat is doing well at her sister’s. She asked about the order. I told her nothing yet. She said the landlord’s agent called her yesterday and offered to let her pick up her belongings if she signed a release saying she “voluntarily surrendered” the unit. I told her not to sign anything and to refer the agent to me. She said she would. I called D. Simmons and left a message saying any communication should go through our office.

2024-02-27 – 14:20 – RO
Checked docket at 2:00 p.m. No order. Also searched for any new filings in the case – none. I will check again tomorrow morning.

2024-02-28 – 10:40 – SW
Client called again. She is anxious. She said she heard from a neighbor that the landlord had someone come and change the locks on the unit. I told her we will address that if the order goes in our favor. She said she is staying with her sister and has no plans to go back to the unit until we say it is okay. I reminded her not to sign anything from Hargrove Properties.

2024-02-28 – 11:05 – RO
Called D. Simmons to ask about the locks. She said the owner changed the locks because the unit was vacant and he wanted to secure it. I told her the client’s belongings are still inside and that changing the locks could be an issue if the court finds the eviction was improper. She said she would pass that along. No further comment.

2024-02-29 – 09:30 – SW
Checked docket at 9:00 a.m. No order yet. Client called at 9:15. She asked if there is a way to speed things up. I explained the judge has five business days and today is day three. She said okay. I told her I would call her the moment we hear anything.

2024-03-01 – 13:45 – RO
Docket check at 1:30 p.m. Still no order. I called the clerk’s office and spoke with M. Tran. She said Judge Alvarez had a heavy calendar this week and the order might come early next week. She noted the deadline is March 5. I thanked her.

2024-03-04 – 10:15 – SW
Client called. She is worried because it has been a week since the hearing. I told her the judge’s deadline is tomorrow and that we should hear something soon. She said she is running out of money and asked about emergency assistance. I gave her the number for the county social services office and told her to mention she is facing possible homelessness. She said she would call.

2024-03-04 – 14:00 – RO
Docket check at 1:45 p.m. No order. I will check again first thing tomorrow.

2024-03-05 – 09:10 – SW
Docket check at 9:00 a.m. Order entered this morning. Judge Alvarez ruled in favor of the client. He found that the landlord failed to follow proper eviction procedure, that the client did not abandon the unit, and that the landlord’s refusal to allow her to retrieve her belongings was unreasonable. He ordered that the client may return to the unit to collect her belongings and that the landlord must allow her access within 48 hours of her request. He did not award damages. I called client and gave her the news. She was very relieved and started to cry. I told her the next step is to request access to the unit.
